title: Concurrent Counter Interleaving & Data Corruption Scenario

candidate.statement: Two worker threads each execute counter += 1 exactly 100,000 times on a shared global variable without synchronization. Explain why the final counter value is typically less than 200,000, detailing the assembly-level read-modify-write race condition.
hints: Break counter += 1 into: load, increment, store.
short_diagnostics: What specific sequence causes an increment operation to be lost?

evaluator.reference_solution: counter += 1 is not atomic; it expands to: (1) load memory into register, (2) add 1 to register, (3) store register to memory. When Thread A and Thread B both load value N before either stores, both compute N+1 and write back N+1. One increment is completely lost. Preemptive context switches cause many updates to be lost, resulting in counter < 200,000.
evaluator.rubric: Identifies non-atomic load-increment-store and traces the interleaved lost-update execution.
known_pitfalls: Believing single high-level statements like counter += 1 are atomic.
evaluator.oracle_notes: Direct scenario reasoning on shared mutable state.
